records.quote: Counterexample 3.1 Consider two series systems, each comprising of three dependent and heterogeneous components with respective survival functions F̄X1:3 (x) = S1 (F̄ (x), α, ϕ1 ) and F̄Y1:3 (x) = S1 (F̄ (x), β, ϕ2 ) with F̄ (x) = e^{−x^{1.5}}, x ≥ 0, α = (2, 3, 5.5), β = (2.5, 3.5, 3.8) so that α ≽^p β. First we take ϕ1 (x) = (2/(1 + e^x))^{1/θ}, θ = 0.9 and ϕ2 (x) = e^{1−(1+x)^{1/η}} with η = 0.3 so that φ2 ◦ ϕ1 is not super additive, and ϕ1 and ϕ2 are not log-convex. We depict F̄X1:3 (x) and F̄Y1:3 (x) in Figure 1 for some finite range of x. From this figure we observe that the stochastic ordering result in Theorem 3.1 is not attained.
records.family: PO model with baseline F̄(x) = e^{−x^{1.5}} (Weibull shape 1.5), two Archimedean survival-copula generators
records.compared: α = (2, 3, 5.5) vs β = (2.5, 3.5, 3.8) satisfying the p-larger order; different generators on the two systems

hypotheses.text: φ2 ◦ ϕ1 is not super additive, and ϕ1 and ϕ2 are not log-convex
hypotheses.formal: the superadditivity and log-convexity hypotheses of Theorem 3.1 dropped

conclusion.direction: no stochastic ordering between X_{1:3} and Y_{1:3}: survival functions cross in Figure 1 — Theorem 3.1 fails without the generator conditions

records.ambiguity: Graphical evidence only. Baseline printed 'e^{−(x)1.5}' in the text layer, interpreted as exp(−x^{1.5}).

note: Both passes agree on substance: st ordering fails without superadditivity/log-convexity; merged record uses B's fuller quote.

records.quote: Counterexample 3.2 Consider two series systems, each comprising of three dependent and heterogeneous components with respective hazard rate functions rX1:3 (x) and rY1:3 (x), with common baseline survival function F̄ (x) = e^{−(0.5x)^2}, x ≥ 0, α = (0.2, 0.4, 0.6), β = (0.35, 0.55, 0.95) so that α ≽^w β. First we take the common generator ϕ(x) = log(e + x)^{−1/a}, a = 0.1, which is not log-concave but ϕ(1−ϕ)/ϕ′ is decreasing and convex. ... From both the figures we observe that the hazard rate ordering result in Theorem 3.3 is not attained.

records.quote: Counterexample 4.1 Consider two parallel systems, each comprising of three dependent and heterogeneous components with respective distribution functions FX3:3 (x) = S2 (F (x), α, ϕ1 ) and FY3:3 (x) = S2 (F (x), β, ϕ2 ), where F (x) = 1 − e^{−x^{0.5}}, x ≥ 0, α = (0.9, 1.45, 2.15), β = (1.2, 1.95, 2.65) so that α ≽^w β. First we take ϕ1 (x) = θ1 / log(x + e^{θ1}) and ϕ2 (x) = e^{1−(1+x)^{1/θ2}} with θ1 = 0.9 and θ2 = 8 so that neither ϕ1 nor ϕ2 is log-concave but φ1 ◦ ϕ2 is super additive. ... the stochastic ordering result in Theorem 4.1 is not attained.

records.quote: Lemma 2.4 [9] For two n-dimensional Archimedean copulas Kϕ1 and Kϕ2 , if φ2 ◦ ϕ1 is superadditive, then Kϕ1 (u) ≤ Kϕ2 (u) for all u ∈ [0, 1]n .
records.family: n-dimensional Archimedean copulas with generators ϕ1, ϕ2

hypotheses.formal: φ2(ϕ1(x+y)) >= φ2(ϕ1(x)) + φ2(ϕ1(y)) (in the superadditive sense used here)

records.ambiguity: Cited from [9] (Li and Fang). Orders two copulas pointwise — in scope per the audit's treatment of copula-ordering lemmas (cf. Lemma A.1 precedents in this batch).

note: Include per precedent: the lemma orders two copulas pointwise (concordance order), the engine for all dependent-case results.
Exclude: conclusion is that S1(x,α,ϕ) is increasing in αi and Schur-concave in α — a monotonicity/Schur property of one function, not a stochastic-order conclusion between two distributions.
Exclude: Lemma 3.2 states I1(u) is increasing and Schur-convex — an analytic property of the hazard multiplier, no ordering conclusion between distributions.
Exclude: Lemma 4.1 states S2(x,α,ϕ) decreasing in αi and Schur-convex — a monotonicity/Schur property, not an ordering conclusion.
